components.name: Chart

A figure with its title and takeaway, the drawing from whichever adapter the registry picks for the kind, the colour key, a caption (what a unit means, when, where from, how sure) and, under it, the same numbers as a table that starts closed. The spec is checked first, so a chart that does not add up is an error and never a wrong picture.

components.name: ScaledBreakdown
components.description: A breakdown chart drawn in the browser with every amount multiplied by `factor` (#1020): the City's tax on the home a reader typed, split the way the budget is. It is the same figure as `Chart` draws for a breakdown (title, takeaway, the drawing, the caption) from the same drawing code, but it takes a spec that was already checked on the server and never parses it, so no spec rules (zod) and no chart library reach the browser; `ScaledBreakdown.test.tsx` guards that. Every figure is text in the drawing, so it has no separate numbers table. Each time `fillKey` changes (a row that holds it opening), the bars grow and the amounts count up from nothing, while the percents stay put; `compact` draws thinner bars, for a breakdown inside a bill (#1163).

The bars share one scale, the largest slice's, and every row is built the same way, so the rows and bars sit level. The receipt is one grid of three columns with fixed widths for the percent and the amount, so each column lines up from row to row and the block keeps its height when the amounts change. The total flashes the accent once each time `pulseKey` changes, unless motion is reduced. The caller writes `label`, the name the list has for screen readers (the list's name). `nested` puts extra content, such as an open-and-close row about one slice, as a row of its own directly under that slice's row, indented to its name (#1163).

The article flow already spaces its children, so the block opts out of the `prose` typography styles (their `picture` margins) and sets one margin, the shared `FIGURE_GAP`, which a legend under the image takes part of back (#636, #658). A milestone's status shows three ways: the marker's shape (filled, ringed, dashed, hollow), the line to it (solid once reached, dashed ahead) and a labelled badge, so it reads without colour. The markers and line are decoration; the list, dates, titles and badges carry the meaning for screen readers.

On wide screens the outcomes sit side by side under the question, joined by a stem and a bar; on phones they stack, hung from a line down the left. The connectors are decoration: the question is a heading and the outcomes a list, each title read with its tone in words ("Goes ahead: If they agree"), since the icon is hidden.

components.description: A row of small fact cards (#509, #660), after the USWDS icon list and summary box: an icon beside what the fact is, a big short value, how sure we are in words, and the source (`FactCard`). In the shared `CardGrid`, a list, so screen readers hear how many facts there are. The cards share their rows (subgrid), so the values and sources line up even when one title wraps (#678). The row gap is zero because a shared row's gap would sit between a card's own rows: each card keeps its distance from the next one below with a bottom margin, which the list's negative margin takes back at the end.

components.name: FactCard
components.description: One fact as a small card (#509, #660, #674): the icon beside what the fact is about, in bold body-size text, on the first row; the big short value under it; an optional one-line explanation; then how sure we are in words and the source. The same order on screen and for screen readers (`dt`, then `dd`s). The icon sits inside the `dt`, decorative, and aligned to the label's first line so a label that wraps doesn't centre it awkwardly. Drawn here so the key facts row and any later block that shows a fact look the same. `variant="tab"` (#664, #1112) is the face of a tab button: only the label shows, in phrasing elements, since the tab button is the box (its border, selected state and focus ring), and with no link, because a link can't sit inside a button. The tab's figure and how sure we are are visually hidden text after the label, so screen readers still hear them from the button; the open panel shows both (`FactTabs`). With a `tabId`, `{yearly}` and `{monthly}` in the figure follow the tab's whole tax bill (#1029).

props.name: tabId
props.doc: The tab this button opens, so a `{yearly}` in its figure follows the tab's whole bill (#1029)

components.name: FactTabs
components.description: Key facts that open pictures (#664): each fact is a tab button (`FactCard` as a tab) that shows its heading, definition and charts or timelines. `Tabs` renders every panel on the server and shows one at a time only when scripting is on, so with it off the panels read stacked, each under its heading. A tab with no renderable picture still shows its definition.

components.name: SectionTabs
components.description: An article split into tabs of ordinary content (#1333): the shared `Tabs` (equal label-only buttons in one row, the content directly under them in the same column, every panel on the server so with scripting off they read one after another under their labels). The content of a tab arrives drawn, so this knows nothing of rich text. It clears any floated picture before it, so the buttons and what they open stay in one column under an introduction and its picture. It is not `not-prose`: the content of a tab is article text, and Tailwind's typography skips everything under a `not-prose` ancestor, even a nested `prose`.

components.name: FilledText
components.description: A tab's text with `{yearly}` and `{monthly}` written out for the home and year shown. Text without them, or in a tab with no whole tax bill, shows as written. `keepLastWords` ties the last two words (a tab button's figure, #707).

components.name: BillShare
components.description: The whole property-tax bill at the top of a fact tab (#1018, #1111), one column on every width, in the order a neighbor needs it: the bill block's one intro line, the Rough Estimator (the home value the reader can change, which starts at the City's average home, and the switch between tax years), the answer card (the City's tax on the home and year, its increase, the year's status), the whole bill (its own card: the total, one bar whose slices are as wide as their shares, and the receipt naming each, with where the City's share goes (the split alone) as a closed row under the City's own row, #1163), then one card of two rows: why the bill may differ and the sources. The tab's other pictures (`children`) follow. Everything is drawn again for every home value and year, so every amount is the City's slice of the bill. A year in which a body has not set its rate uses that body's rate from the year before, and says so on its line in the rates panel and in the toast its Estimate button opens, so the page never changes height.

components.name: BillAnswer
components.description: The answer a neighbor came for (#1111, #1118), right under the Rough Estimator. Its top row has the label on the left ("City tax on an average home", or "on your home" after an estimate) and the status badge on the right. Under it the City's tax on the home last estimated in the year chosen is the biggest text on the tab, with a small "a year", then the City's increase in the estimator's accent, orange (`increaseLine`, the same figures a tab's `{yearly}` and `{monthly}` use, so they always agree) and, while the card shows the City's average home, one small sentence with that home's value and the City's share of the whole bill. After an estimate the sentence is left out: it would only repeat the value the reader typed and a share the whole bill shows (#1183). The badge is the Estimate button, there in every year: the card only knows the average home, not the credits, exemptions or kind of property that change a real bill (#1417). The increase line keeps its room when there is no figure, so the card never changes height. In the earliest of several years it reads "Base year" in the primary green instead, with the next year's line kept as hidden room (#1135). It draws what it is given.

props.name: baseYear
props.doc: Whether the year is the earliest of several: the line says "Base year", the one the later year is compared with (#1135)

props.name: laterIncrease
props.doc: In the base year: the next year's increase, whose line is kept as hidden room so the card is as tall in both years

props.name: onBadgePress

components.name: RatesPanel
components.description: The rates the bill is worked out from (#1351), beside the answer card: one line per body with its name and the year its rate is from on the left, and its rate as a percent with the same rate in dollars per $1,000 of value on the right. The City's line is highlighted, since the tab is about the City's tax. Every line is built the same way and as tall as the others, so the lines sit level in every year and the panel never changes height; a body with no rate keeps its line, with "No rate yet" in place of the figures. The year each rate is from is on every line, so the panel never depends on the toast (`toast`, #1380) that says why: the page puts it over the panel's top edge (the card is its positioned container), where it covers a sliver and takes no room, so the panel is as tall in every year. It draws what it is given. Its title is the same header style as the other two panels', and its status badge sits at the end of the title's line, a button that opens the toast when it has something to say (#1417).

components.name: PanelHeader
components.description: The top line of a whole-bill panel (#1417): its title on the left and, when it has one, the status badge at the end of the same line, level with the title's first line; a title too long to share the line puts the badge under it, at its start. The answer card, the rates panel and the whole bill share the line (`PANEL_TITLE_ROW`), so they can never differ.

components.name: StatusBadgeButton
components.description: The tab's status badge as the whole-bill panels draw it (#1417): small, a button when it has something to say

components.name: BillDetails
components.description: The two rows under the whole bill (#1111, #1118, #1163), in one card split by divider lines: why the real bill may differ (the notes, then the tab's short text and detail) and the sources, each source once, both closed when the tab loads, each titled from the block (#1158). Where the City's share goes is a row of the whole bill itself, under the City's row (`BillShare`, #1163). The sources row (the as-of line of the City's breakdown, then each link) is left out when there is neither, and a note that is not showing still takes its room, hidden from everyone, so an open row never changes height when a year is chosen. Each row is the kit's `Disclosure`, so it opens and closes without scripting and never moves what is above it.

components.name: BreakdownRow
components.description: Where the City's tax goes, as a closed row of the whole bill under the City's own row (#1163): the split alone, with thin bars, since the answer card above already gives the City's tax and its increase and the row's title is the heading (#1144). Its date and sources are not drawn here: the whole bill's Sources row lists them (#1180). `row` is `useBreakdownAutoOpen`'s: it opens the row after each estimate that changes the bill while it is closed (#1176), and each opening fills the bars again (#1165).

components.name: NoteText
components.description: A note's text with its link drawn where the editor wrote `{link}`. A blank with no link to draw (a draft Admin did not check) is left out, so readers never see it; a link with no blank to stand in is not drawn, and a second blank draws nothing (Admin refuses both on save).

components.name: RoughEstimator
components.description: The tool at the top of a whole-bill picture (#1022): a compact orange card, named Rough Estimator for screen readers but with no title drawn, with the home value box and, on the same row at every width, the tax years as one joined two-option control of the year numbers, as tall as the box (#1118). The box has a check-mark button inside it at its end (#1110): off, flat and muted, while the typed value is not a new number, and on, accent-colored and slightly raised once it is (Enter in the box does the same), so on a phone it sits right above the keyboard (#1087). Nothing is drawn under the years: the answer card's badge says a year's status. It draws what it is given and keeps no state of its own.

components.name: BillFiguresProvider
components.description: Shares each tab's City figures between its button and its heading, which sit apart in the tab list and the panel (#1029). The whole bill in a panel reports the figures for the home estimated and the year chosen; the button and the heading read them. Rendered on the server with the average home's figures, so nothing flashes wrong before scripts run.
